themes: New capacity and new money (Birla Opus, JSW Dulux)

Grasim's Birla Opus (launched Feb-2024) was the #3 organised decorative player by Q1FY27 with revenue of Rs1,661 cr (+64% YoY) and 1,450+ franchise outlets; its share rose ~30 bp QoQ and, with Birla White putty, is 'nearing early teens' (Grasim, Aug-2026). JSW Paints took control of Akzo Nobel India (now JSW Dulux) in 2025. Asian Paints says discounting has seen 'no let-up' and intensity is 'at an all-time high'.

Elara (via Reuters): Asian Paints' share of branded decorative paints fell from 59% to 52% in the twelve months to Mar-2025; Systematix (via Outlook Business): 53% (FY23) to 47% (FY25). FY26-Q1FY27 volume growth of 9-12% suggests the loss has slowed; management says it grew 'slightly higher than the industry' in Q1FY27. No audited share data exist.

For two years value growth trailed volume by 4-7 points (price cuts, down-trading to putty and economy emulsions, higher rebates). In Q1FY27 value (+16.6%) ran ahead of volume (+9%) because of price increases. Management expects value > volume 'till the time we get into pricing corrections'.

Material inflation ~20-25% from Mar-2026 against ~11% price increases by May and ~13-14% by June; Q1FY27 margins were protected by low-cost inventory, Q2 carries the higher cost. TiO2 (largest input, not crude-linked) started rising at end-June while monomers eased.
Rural and T3/T4 towns ahead of large cities; B2B (factories, government, hospitality projects) strong. Management guides 8-10% FY27 decorative volume growth.

VAM-VAE (Dahej, ~Rs3,250 cr) starting Aug-2026: 300-500 bp gross-margin benefit on products using in-house emulsion, ramping over 2-2.5 years; white cement (Fujairah) operational. Rivals buy these inputs.
CCI DG investigation (ordered 1-Jul-2025) into alleged abuse of dominance on Grasim's complaint; penalties under the Competition Act can go up to 10% of turnover.

moat: India's most recognised paint brand; consistent heavy spending (cricket/BCCI, 'Rang De India'); 17% of revenue from products launched in the last three years.
Pricing power at the premium end; weaker in economy products where contractors switch for discounts.
~1.7 lakh retail touchpoints, 6,000+ added in FY26; Birla Opus built 1,450+ franchise outlets and a large dealer base within two years by offering higher dealer margins and schemes.
The network was the moat; it proved replicable with money. Asian Paints still has the deepest reach.
27 plants, 1.85 mn KL capacity; in the 2026 supply shock large players gained share from small ones (management, brokers).
Lowest cost to serve; resilience in shocks.
VAM-VAE (Dahej) and white cement (Fujairah): 300-500 bp gross-margin benefit on products using in-house VAE, ramping over 2-2.5 years.
Unique among Indian paint makers; benefits are a few years out and partly offset by start-up costs.
'World's largest' home-painting service (Beautiful Homes); 9+ lakh painters trained.
Kitchen, bath, White Teak and Weatherseal together ~Rs920 cr of revenue (FY26), loss-making or near break-even; White Teak impaired twice.
Capital spent without returns so far.
critiques: Share loss is structural: Birla Opus is #3 within ~2.5 years and still gaining ~30 bp a quarter; JSW now owns Dulux. A 50%+ share will not return
PL, Macquarie, HSBC; Elara data via Reuters
Q1FY27 margins were flattered by low-cost inventory; with ~25% inflation against ~8-9% price, Q2 margins fall and the 18-20% band may hold only if crude eases
Discounting has not eased even as prices rose: dealer and contractor schemes are the real price, and they are not falling
FY27 revenue growth is mostly price; when inputs fall, prices come back down (management has flagged possible H2 cuts) and FY28 growth slows sharply
Nomura and Elara argue the worst of the price war is over as Birla Opus turns to profitability, and share loss is in the past
Capital allocation outside paints (White Teak, Weatherseal, bath, kitchens) has destroyed value; Rs3,250 cr VAM-VAE and Rs2,000 cr MP plant raise capital intensity
At ~40x our FY28E EPS the stock still prices a dominant franchise; the street's 50x FY28E multiple is the stock's old pre-competition level
CCI investigation: an adverse finding could bring a penalty and curbs on dealer practices
gaps: The company reports no segments; decorative India revenue and EBITDA are not disclosed. The standalone entity (~97% decorative) is used as the proxy.
International, APPPG, kitchen, bath, White Teak and Weatherseal EBITDA are not disclosed (PBT only, some quarters only); the subsidiaries line is modelled as one block.
Decorative value growth for Q1-Q3FY25 and FY25 standalone gross margins by quarter were read from deck charts (values) or not collected.
Audited market-share data do not exist; the 59%→52% (Elara) and 53%→47% (Systematix) estimates use different definitions.
Birla Opus FY26 revenue and profitability were not collected; Grasim does not disclose paints EBITDA.
